newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan Taleban ask Red Cross help on war prisoners.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban ask Red Cross help on war prisoners.

text.p: The purist Islamic Taleban on Monday called on the international community to pressure the opposition alliance to allow the International Committee of the Red Cross to visit Taleban prisoners.

"The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) has been trying to get access to the prisoners held by the opposition for a long time. So far their efforts have failed, they have not been able to see them, let alone provide other assistance," Taleban interior minister Mullah Khairullah Khairkhwa told reporters in Kabul on Monday evening.
"We criticise these organisations (ICRC and the United Nations) for their continued silence on this problem," said Khairkhwa.
He said that the Taleban had allowed the ICRC free access to all the prisons in the areas of Afghanistan under its control.
No ICRC official was available for comment on Monday night.
Khairkhwa accused the opposition fighters loyal to General Abdul Malik, leader of one of the three parties in the opposition alliance, of killing Taleban prisoners.
"We have clear evidence that Malik's men are daily taking out five or 10 prisoners and shooting them dead. The evidence comes from one Taleb who escaped the massacre," said Khairkhwa.
There has been no independent confirmation of the allegations.
The fundamentalist Taleban movement controls two-thirds of Afghanistan, including Kabul, but the so-called Northern Alliance has advanced to within 12 miles (20 km) of the capital.
Khairkhwa said that while the world was watching the Taleban closely, the opposition was committing human rights abuses without any censure.
He was particularly critical of the human rights organisation Amnesty International, which issued a statement 11 days ago accusing the Taleban of arresting 2,000 Kabul residents on ethnic grounds.
The Taleban denied the Amnesty accusations and the ICRC said at the time that as far as they were aware the numbers of people arrested in Kabul were "substantially lower".

"We criticise Amnesty International, which is looking so hard at problems in the Taleban-controlled areas of Afghanistan. But there is this blatant violation of human rights in the north and they have kept silent about it," said Khairkhwa.

Many of the prisoners held by the opposition in northern Afghanistan were captured after the Taleban's abortive attempt to take the northern stronghold of Mazar-i-Sharif went desperately wrong in late May.
Hundreds of Taleban were killed in the streets of the town, but many more were captured, including the governor of Herat province and the governor of the central bank.
